chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Safwan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:
I asked Aba Ibrahim عليه السلام about a person with a broken limb who has splints upon him: how should he perform wudu (ablution), ghusl (ritual bath) of janabah, and ghusl (ritual bath) of Friday?

He عليه السلام said: "He washes whatever he can reach of what is exposed, from that over which there are no splints; and he leaves aside the rest of that which cannot be washed. He should not remove the splints, nor should he tamper with his wound."

key_terms.الْجَبَائِرُ: splints or bandages placed over an injury
key_terms.الْكَسِيرِ: a person with a broken limb or injury
key_terms.غُسْلِ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janabah
key_terms.لَا يُسْتَطَاعُ غَسْلُهُ: that which cannot be washed due to inability
key_terms.يَغْسِلُ: he washes the part he is able to wash

ai.seo_question: How should an injured person with bandages or splints perform wudu (ablution) and ghusl (ritual bath)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for ritual purification when a person has an injury covered by splints or bandages. It instructs him to wash the exposed parts he can reach and leave what cannot be washed, without removing the splints or disturbing the wound.
